extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, reviewers, and students interested in open peer review and scholarly publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and guidance on open peer review (OPR) models: definitions, core elements, benefits and challenges, and types of peer review for researchers, journals, and institutions considering or participating in OPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review goals: validity, originality, rigorous evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is the process adopted to guarantee published research is valid, original and rigorously evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review to assess whether research findings are valid (methodologically and factually sound), original (novel contribution), and evaluated rigorously (thorough scrutiny of methods, analyses, and claims). These are the foundational quality aims against which review processes are judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional peer review characteristics: anonymous, confidential, selective
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional peer review practices (often 'blind') are anonymous, confidential, and selective: reviews and author responses are not accessible to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that many journals maintain confidentiality and anonymity to protect reviewers; this model emphasizes privacy and selection by editors rather than public transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-blind review: reviewers know the authors' identities, but reviewer names are protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common traditional model; can allow reviewer bias based on author identity but protects reviewers from direct attribution in the published decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymized (double-blind) review
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-anonymized review: reviewer and author names are protected (neither party knows the other's identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reduce bias based on author identity (affiliation, reputation, etc.), though true anonymization can be difficult in specialized fields or when preprints exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Peer Review (general definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review (OPR) is an umbrella term for various combinations of open practices in the review process in pursuit of increased transparency and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPR can be implemented in different combinations (see the seven core elements). It is not a single fixed model but a set of practices intended to increase openness in review workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and reviewers are aware of each other’s identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revealing identities aims to increase accountability and credit but may discourage candid criticism and raise concerns about retaliation or career consequences for reviewers, especially junior researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Review reports are published alongside the relevant article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing review reports provides transparency about the review content and rationale for editorial decisions; it can serve as training material and evidence of review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The wider community is able to contribute to the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing broader community input (e.g., public commenting) can increase inclusivity and surface diverse perspectives, but moderation and quality-control mechanisms may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct reciprocal discussion between author(s) and reviewers, and/or between reviewers, is allowed and encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates constructive dialogue, clarification, and faster resolution of issues; can reduce inconsistency and confusion in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open pre-review manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are made immediately available (e.g., via preprint servers like arXiv) in advance of formal peer review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints accelerate dissemination and allow early community feedback before or during formal review; journals adopting this should consider policies for preprint citation and versioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open final version commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing or commenting on final ‘version of record’ publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables post-publication scrutiny and ongoing discussion of the published record; requires platforms or journal systems to host and moderate comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open platforms (decoupled review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is facilitated by a different organisational entity than the venue of publication ('decoupled review').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating review services from publication venues can enable portability and new workflows (e.g., independent review platforms), but raises coordination and recognition considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased transparency and accountability (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the review process becomes transparent, including the review reports and reviewer identities, reviewers are more accountable for their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency can help prevent conflicts of interest and biased or inaccurate reviews; evaluating OPR should consider whether these transparency mechanisms actually reduce bias and improve accountability in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: More constructive and efficient quality assurance (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revealing review contents and reviewer identities may drive reviewers to make more constructive feedback and provide more substantiating evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct communications between authors and reviewers can enhance clarity, reduce inconsistency and confusion, and save time; assess whether OPR implementations lead to higher-quality, evidence-backed reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wider and more inclusive discussion (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open commenting enables the wider research community to comment and engage in constructive dialogue, facilitating more inclusive discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether open participation truly broadens engagement across career stages, geographies and perspectives, and whether moderation supports productive discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of training opportunity and professional development (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since review reports are openly accessible, they could be a training opportunity for early career researchers who may be less experienced in conducting reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open reports can be used as exemplars for learning to review; institutions and journals can encourage use of open reviews in reviewer training programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased reviewers' incentive for credits (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: When review activities alongside the reviewer’s identity can be made visible and citable, reviewers can receive credits and recognitions that can be added into their profiles and CVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider mechanisms (DOIs for reviews, Publons-like systems) to make review contributions discoverable and creditable when evaluating OPR adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouraging honest feedback (challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers’ identities and their review reports are openly published, there are concerns that reviewers may tend to be less critical and more hesitant to provide candid feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether openness reduces critical rigor; journals may need policies that balance transparency with protections for candid critique (e.g., optional signing, protected channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of reviewer retaliation (challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may fear retaliation if they have given an unfavourable review with their names visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly affects early career researchers who may hesitate to critique senior researchers; consider safeguards, mentoring, or opt-in policies to mitigate retaliation risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concerns on threats of negative career consequences (challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may worry about negative career consequences from critical reviews or inappropriate comments in an open model, especially junior researchers dependent on senior scientists for opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should consider moderation, codes of conduct, and dispute resolution processes to protect authors (and reviewers) from unfair or harmful public commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed review (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers sign their comments. Authors receive reviewer names in the decision letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed reviews make reviewer identities public to authors (and sometimes readers); evaluate effects on review candour and reviewer willingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative review (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers collaborate and submit joint comments, or in some cases confer with authors and editors during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes consensus-building and comprehensive feedback; may require coordination and clear attribution of contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable review (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are sought by an organization or journal and shared with any journals that require them later on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables efficiency across journals (e.g., transfer of reviewer reports), but requires interoperability and agreements on reuse of reports and reviewer consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published review (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments and/or names are published with the article or preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing comments increases transparency and provides a permanent record of the review discourse; consider formatting, linking, and indexing of published reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication review (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a manuscript is posted the community reviews the research in an open forum. Reviewer names are usually published with their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts review from pre-publication gatekeeping to ongoing public evaluation; requires moderation, curation, and mechanisms to surface high-quality commentary.
